verdict.rationale: Box documents collaborations that grant users and groups role-based access to individual files and folders, working like ACLs. A community user confirms selectively granting outside parties access to files and folders. However, the evidence never lists the specific roles (viewer/commenter/editor/owner) and never describes how permissions inherit down folder trees. Missing for 10: an enumerated role list with per-role permissions, documented folder-to-subfolder/file inheritance behavior.

support.subject: As an IT admin, permissions are granular — folder- and file-level roles (viewer/commenter/editor/owner) with inheritance behavior documented

citations.quote: Collaborations define access permissions for users and groups on files and folders, similar to access control lists.
A collaboration object grants a user or group access to a file or folder with permissions defined by a specific role.
Grant users and groups role-based access to files and folders
it's possible to selectively grant outside parties access to files/folders.
